answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the mirror index resolves every citation against the nectar checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the echo audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 128 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 128 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 16 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
